claim_one_line: B1164's observer-freedom census (2 discrete + 1 continuous, ALL ARCHIMEDEAN, claimed as 'the whole program's observer freedom') and the banked final-price ledger (one unit, two bits, one orbit-point) DISAGREE BY TWO ITEMS. Matching: scale<->unit, orientation<->chirality. MISSING FROM B1164: time's arrow (grep 'arrow|time' = 0 hits) and the VEV orbit-point (grep 'VEV|orbit-point|F4(Z)|Krutelevich' = 0 hits). NEW IN B1164, absent from the price ledger: D2 = sqrt(3). The orbit-point is booked as FINITE OVER Z -- a non-archimedean cost -- which would falsify B1164's 'everything the observer supplies is archimedean' if it is a genuine observer cost.
creates_law: TWO LEDGERS OF THE SAME PRICE MUST BE RECONCILED OR ONE MUST BE WITHDRAWN. Exactly one of these holds: (1) the price ledger OVER-COUNTS because the arrow and the orbit-point were discharged after 2026-08-11 -- in which case the campaign is cheaper than banked and that good news is currently invisible; or (2) B1164's census UNDER-COUNTS -- in which case 'the whole program's observer freedom = archimedean data' must narrow to 'the archimedean part of it'. SCOPE: this arc asserts NEITHER. It establishes only that both cannot stand as written.
